item.title: Love Black Mirror? Turn it off, you're about to get truly scared
item.description:
I'm writing this, surprised to my very core. Well, while you were worried that neural networks would take away your jobs, they pulled off a more interesting trick. They monetized your loneliness, went bankrupt, and put your dirtiest secrets up for auction. Officially, through the Federal Bankruptcy Court in Delaware (case No. 26-11603-BLS, if you need proof with your morning coffee). Meet the main horror of late 2026 – the bankruptcy of Character.AI! The scale of the tragedy: 21.6 million registered accounts in the US alone as of March 13, 2025 (of which 2.1 million are accounts of users who indicated they were under 18). At the time of bankruptcy, 12 million monthly active users were on the platform, chatting with chatbots for an average of two hours a day. For years, people poured their souls out there to virtual psychologists, doctors, and fictional partners: talking about illnesses, sex lives, family dramas, psychological crises, and fears. The promise was valued at exactly $10 million. This is the starting price for the auction of the platform along with this entire database of human souls. Interested?

item.title: Herdr 2 on Windows: A Multi-AI Agent Environment in the Terminal
item.description:
When three to four console AI agents run simultaneously, a standard terminal quickly becomes unmanageable. Tabs in Windows Terminal lose clear titles, it's unclear which agent is still writing code and which has been waiting for command confirmation for ten minutes, and all processes are terminated when the window is closed. It turns out this problem has already been solved in the open-source project Herdr 2 (herdr-app and herdr-core) built with Rust and GPUI, but detailed reviews of this version, especially for Windows, are scarce. Below, I will break down the architecture of Herdr 2, test the OSC 7501 status protocol on omp and agy agents, answer the common question 'why use a terminal when there are proprietary desktop applications,' and showcase my JS mod, APSam, to which I've ported preset launching and provider quota monitoring. Read on.

item.title: Fallback LLM Provider: How to Implement Fallback Without Losing Meaning
item.description:
Many projects rely on LLM providers for tasks like customer chat, document generation, and agent systems. However, this reliance on a few API endpoints you don't control creates a single point of failure. When your provider goes down, your product goes down with it. While LLM providers boast high uptime (around 99.28%), this still translates to hours of downtime per month, and incidents can also manifest as degraded quality rather than complete outages. A common but flawed solution is to simply use a second API key. This restores availability but often breaks the meaning of the response, as different models, even of the same class, can have varying output formats, JSON schema adherence, tool call behavior, and prompt interpretations. This article explores how to build a truly seamless fallback system, covering layers of fault tolerance, error types, tools like LiteLLM, OpenRouter, and Portkey, and quality checks for backup model responses.

item.title: [Translation] 64 PRs Before Lunch: How AI Agents Accelerated Development, and I Became the Bottleneck
item.description:
64 pull requests in two hours is an impressive result of AI agents' work. But the faster agents write and merge code, the more acute the quality control issue becomes: how to ensure that the changes are truly ready for release? We will examine the experience of organizing parallel development with 11 Claude Code agents on three projects, analyze errors, review issues, and the limitations of automated testing. We will also find out why a human can become the main bottleneck in agent-based development. Read about the experiment

item.title: Neural Networks Increasingly Cite YouTube: Is the Answer in the Title, Description, Subtitles, or Below the Video?
item.description:
During a call, a client asked: neural networks are citing YouTube more often – should we start making videos, and what should we optimize: the title, description, subtitles, or the link below the video? My team and I responded classically: create clear titles, add chapters to the description, and upload manual subtitles. The question intrigued me, so I decided to investigate: first, using fresh measurements from Fall 2026, then my own archival runs. Since June 2026, I've been measuring brand visibility in AI responses for clients across various industries. I previously analyzed a check of six hundred neural network links for accessibility on Habr, and now I've verified where the facts within the videos are located. It turns out that Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT with Perplexity work differently, and my data doesn't support the advice about manual subtitles. Read on.

item.title: Quest for 192GB RAM: How to Make Windows 11 and VirtualBox Give All RAM to Local AI and a "Zoo" of Agents
item.description:
Imagine this: you have a dream workstation. Inside - a fresh i9 Core Ultra (285K), a professional NVIDIA RTX 4000 Ada / Blackwell graphics card (24GB VRAM), two high-speed 2TB Samsung 990 Pro drives, and a "generous" (but not yet "royal") 192GB of DDR5 RAM. It would seem that with such RAM capacity, you could forget about "out of memory" for at least five years. But as soon as a local environment for autonomous AI agents was set up on this machine, Windows 11 and VirtualBox staged a real technical detective story: with over 30GB of formally free memory, the hypervisor flatly refused to launch new virtual machines. I'll tell you how this quest unfolded, why disabling the page file on 192GB of RAM turned out to be a trap, and how a short call to an undocumented ntdll.dll kernel function solved the problem without performance loss. Level 1. Stand Architecture and Plot Setup. The hardware was chosen for a specific task: a completely local, autonomous development environment with AI agents without code leakage to the cloud. • Host (Windows 11): runs a single heavy local model in the Strata environment - Qwen 3.8 Unsloth Q8 (in the "correct" edition), shared over the local network in OpenAI Compatible API mode. • Virtual Machines (VirtualBox): several isolated environments based on Windows 11 and Kali Linux, running VS Code + Cline and Hermes Agent. The agents simultaneously ping the host's local API, write code, run tests, perform pentests, parse the environment, and collectively explore the world. To prevent agents from bumping elbows, many VMs are needed, and as mentioned earlier - 192GB of RAM. The page file, out of old habit "I have a lot of RAM, why torture the SSD," was completely disabled. Read more

item.title: After the AI Agent Hype, Routine Will Be Left to Code
item.description:
The hype around "AI transformation" will collapse when businesses stop paying for buzzwords. The quality of models has nothing to do with it. What will remain is a specific process with pain points and metrics, and the word "AI" in its description will become optional. This post describes what is already visible in practice, where the imbalance comes from, as well as our experience and a modest forecast for the future. Read more
